steps.title: Measure growth, not seconds
steps.content: Time complexity describes how an algorithm's work grows as input size n grows. Big O focuses on an upper-bound growth rate and ignores constant factors and lower-order terms.
steps.example: 3n + 10 grows linearly, so it is O(n).

steps.title: Recognize a linear loop
steps.prompt: A loop visits each of n array elements once. What is its time complexity?
steps.explanation: The number of iterations grows proportionally to n.

steps.title: Recognize nested loops
steps.content: Two independent loops each running n times produce about n×n operations, or O(n²). A loop that repeatedly halves n takes O(log n) iterations.
steps.example: for i in range(n): for j in range(n): work() is O(n²).

steps.title: Analyze a halving loop
steps.prompt: A loop starts with n and halves the value each iteration until it reaches 1. What is its complexity?
steps.explanation: The number of halvings needed to reach 1 is approximately log₂(n).

steps.title: Compare common growth rates
steps.content: For large n, O(1) grows slowest, then O(log n), O(n), O(n log n), O(n²) and O(2^n). Analyze the dominant operation and remember that input structure can affect an algorithm's best and worst cases.
steps.tip: State the input size and whether you are discussing best, average or worst case.

questions.prompt: What is the time complexity of reading an array element by index?
questions.explanation: Array indexing uses direct address calculation and is constant time.

questions.prompt: Two nested loops each run n times. What is the total complexity?
questions.explanation: The inner work runs n times for each of n outer iterations.

questions.prompt: Which grows faster for large n?
options: They grow at the same rate
questions.explanation: Linear growth eventually exceeds logarithmic growth.

questions.prompt: What is the time complexity of merge sort?
questions.explanation: Merge sort divides the array into log n levels and processes n items per level.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of dropping constants in Big O?
options: To describe the dominant growth rate
questions.explanation: Big O emphasizes how growth changes with input size, not machine-specific constants.
